chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about some people who claimed that a slave belonging to a man had committed an offense against a man, one that would encompass his neck, and the slave confessed to it.

He عليه السلام said: "The confession of the slave is not valid against his master. If they establish proof for what they claimed against the slave, they may take the slave for it, or his master may ransom him."

key_terms.تُحِيطُ بِرَقَبَتِهِ: an offense entailing full liability upon the person of the slave
key_terms.جِنَايَةً: a criminal offense or injurious act
key_terms.فَأَقَرَّ: he confessed or acknowledged the claim

ai.seo_question: Is a slave’s confession legally binding upon his master in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slave accused of a grave offense. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that the slave’s confession does not bind the master, and that liability is established only through proof; if proven, the slave may be taken for the offense or the master may redeem him.
